title: Preflight readiness & hotpatch rotation - June 2026 (WIP)
content:
Context:
This doc is a working artifact for the upcoming June release window. It mixes the release preflight checklist, a compact rollout calendar (including hotpatch rotation and on-call handoffs), and a first-pass customer-facing release notes draft. Audience: release engineers, SREs, on-call, and product PMs.

1) Quick summary (for execs & PMs)
- Ship target: feature set v1.18 (platform + serving runtime tweaks, proactive caching).
- Risk profile: medium (changes to batching heuristics + one infra migration).
- Target rollout: staged over 3 days with an 8-hour observation window per stage.

2) Preflight readiness checklist (do not skip)
- Code / artifacts
  - [ ] All PRs merged to release branch; verify no pending dependency bumps (owner: Maya).
  - [ ] Release tag created and pushed (v1.18.0-rc1).
  - [ ] Build artifacts available in internal registry and checksum verified.
  - [ ] Docker images scanned (Snyk) and cleared for CVEs > critical.

- Tests & quality
  - [ ] Nightly integration run green for last 48 hours (include long-tail seq tests).
  - [ ] End-to-end smoke tests (serving runtime) pass locally and in staging.
  - [ ] Performance baseline measured: p50/p95/p99 latency aligned with SLO delta acceptance.
  - [ ] Load tests for new batching heuristics: 2x peak simulated for 30m.

- Infra & deployment
  - [ ] Migration plan for KV cache index schema reviewed and approved (SRE).
  - [ ] DB migrations scoped to non-blocking, can be rolled back within 15 minutes.
  - [ ] Capacity check: dedicated GPU pool quotas validated for expected increase.
  - [ ] Region routing config ready; fallback routes defined for each region.

- Observability & runbooks
  - [ ] Dashboards for token-level cost and latency ready and pinned.
  - [ ] Alert thresholds agreed: latency spike, error rate > 0.5% per minute, p95 degradation.
  - [ ] Post-deploy runbook updated with triage owners and escalation matrix.
  - [ ] Canary health checks defined: connectivity, kv-hit-rate, response correctness.

- Communication
  - [ ] Slack channel #release-v1-18 created and invited: eng, sre, product, pm.
  - [ ] Customer-facing status template drafted for potential incidents.
  - [ ] Release window announced to internal teams and CS with rollback plan.

Notes-to-self: double-check the migration id referenced in the PR (local dev used migration-1b). If mismatch, might block automatic rollbacks.

3) Rollout calendar (compact view)
- Day 0 (2026-06-22): Pre-release checklist & final tag
  - 09:00: Release kickoff call (15m) - owners: Maya + Arjun
  - 09:30-11:00: Bake artifacts into staging, run quick smoke and perf checks
  - 11:30: Final sign-off meeting (PM + SRE)
  - 12:00: Start of maintenance window (announce)

- Day 1 (2026-06-23): Stage A - internal staging -> canary region
  - 02:00: Deploy to Canary region A (10% traffic)
  - 02:10-10:10: Observation window (8h). Monitor kv-hit-rate, p95 latency, error rate.
  - 10:30: If stable, promote to Region B at 30% traffic
  - 11:00-19:00: Observation window (8h). If issues -> rollback to previous tag and trigger hotpatch rotation.

- Day 2 (2026-06-24): Stage B - global progressive rollout
  - 01:00: Deploy to remaining regions in parallel up to 60% traffic per region with progressive steps (60->80->100).
  - Rolling observation after each increment: short 1h windows at each step, then 4h final watch.
  - 20:00: Expected end of major rollout. Begin long-tail monitoring.

- Hotpatch & rollback rotation (on-call schedule)
  - If a production blocking issue is detected during any observation window:
    - Immediate action: scale down traffic to safe tier and trigger rollback to previous tag.
    - Hotpatch rotation: primary on-call (Ethan Park) + release lead (Maya) + SRE (Arjun) form triage.
    - Cold swap time target: 20 min; full rollback target: 45 min.
  - On-call handoffs: 8-hour shifts for the 48h post-rollout period. Shift owners appended in schedule below.

4) Rollback decision matrix (quick reference)
- Severity A (user-facing outage / incorrect outputs): rollback immediately and page on-call.
- Severity B (performance regression > 30% p95 or error rate spike > 1%): hold promotion to next stage, evaluate hotpatch.
- Severity C (non-critical telemetry deviations): continue, file follow-up tickets.

5) Post-release observation & follow-ups
- 48h high-intensity: 8h shifts with quick daily sync (15m) at 09:00 UTC.
- 7-day review: collect perf diffs, customer tickets, infra cost delta, and QA regressions.
- 30-day stability check: determine if heuristic rollbacks or config tuning required.

6) Draft release notes (customer-facing)
- Header: Redwood Inference - Platform Release v1.18 (June 2026)
- TL;DR: Improved serving efficiency and stability — smarter batching heuristics that reduce per-token latency on common workloads and targeted fixes for KV cache edge cases.

- Highlights:
  - Smarter batching: adaptive batching algorithm improves throughput for short-seq workloads, expected unit cost reduction of 8-12% for typical chat loads.
  - KV cache robustness: fixed race condition under heavy concurrent prefix invalidations that could cause stale outputs in <0.01% of requests.
  - Observability improvements: new token-level cost breakdowns in the Console and faster tracing hooks for slow requests.
  - Infra: minor migrations to support regional routing fallbacks (no customer action required).

- Known issues and limitations:
  - In certain high-throughput long-sequence workloads, p99 latency may see transient spikes during the first 30 minutes of rollout as caches warm up. We're monitoring and have mitigations ready.
  - Customers using pinned versions of older runtime images should test against v1.18-rc1 in staging before auto-upgrade.

- For support:
  - Contact: support@redwoodai.example (internal draft address) or open a ticket with priority 'platform-release'.

Notes / TODOs for the release notes:
- Add customer-facing screenshots for the Console token-cost view (Sofia).
- Verify the 8-12% number with bench-run artifacts and link to the perf notebook.
- Decide if wording around "stale outputs" should say "possible inconsistency" or leave as-is. Product prefers transparency but legal review required.

7) Quick checklist for a partial hotpatch (if rollback is not possible)
- Gate: hotpatch only for critical bugfixes that can be applied as a small config/flag change.
- Steps:
  - [ ] Branch from release tag, apply minimal fix, run quick unit+smoke, build artifact.
  - [ ] Run canary health checks on a reduced subset (1 region) for 30 minutes.
  - [ ] If green, roll to remaining regions with 1h watch windows.
  - [ ] Record all steps in incident channel and update release notes with hotpatch details.

8) Misc notes & links
- Related tickets: JIRA-RELEASE-1423, JIRA-ENG-3378 (batching), JIRA-SRE-2111 (cache migration)
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4812 (batching alg), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/909
- Slack threads: #infra-kv-migration, #perf-bench-summaries

9) Open questions / discussion items
- Should we extend the staged observation window from 8h to 12h for regions with historically higher error variance? Pros: catch more regressions early. Cons: slows down rollout and delays customer access.
- Rollforward vs rollback for config-only regressions: what's the preference from SRE/PM?
- Legal wording for release notes around data exposure/stale outputs — need sign-off.

Draft owner notes: This is a living doc. After approval, move the final release note text to the product release page and push the customer-facing announcement. Keep a timeline of who performed each promotion step in the release audit (linked in linked_artifacts).

-- end of doc --
